components.title: Bounded FactoryProduce expansion
components.summary: Validates the uint32 count and actors-times-count as uint64 before int conversion or child allocation, then expands admitted work into count-one children with an upper bound of 64.

components.title: Typed factory policy admission
components.summary: Keeps typed Append, Replace and RejectIfBusy conflict policies while emitting factory native options zero; Replace and RejectIfBusy require an empty complete per-actor production queue.

flows.title: Wide count validation to bounded children

steps.description: Compute per-actor and total child counts in uint64 and require the advertised maximum and total bound of 64 before converting to int.
For every actor, require the exact queue revision and complete queue; Append remains allowed while Replace and RejectIfBusy require no entries.
Translate each admitted child to count one and native BuildUnit options zero while retaining the typed conflict policy.

flows.title: Factory policy and count refusal regression

steps.description: Assert nonempty Replace and RejectIfBusy produce correlated terminal refusals with no native delivery, including multi-actor fail-closed behavior.
Refuse cap-plus-one, zero, UInt32.MaxValue and actors-times-count above 64 before expansion.
Assert Append and empty Replace retain typed conflict policies while emitting options-zero, count-one native children.

facts.statement: FactoryProduce validates positive count, the advertised maximum and actors-times-count no greater than 64 in uint64 before int conversion and child expansion.
Each actor must match the current descriptor and queue revision; one actor whose production queue violates Replace or RejectIfBusy causes the parent to refuse before any delivery.
FactoryProduce translates all admitted policies to native BuildUnit options zero while preserving Append, Replace or RejectIfBusy in the broker conflict policy and tactical action.
The broker regression refuses zero, cap-plus-one, UInt32.MaxValue and a wide multi-actor product before native delivery, and checks complete correlated refusal for nonempty policy conflicts.
These source tests demonstrate broker validation and delivery shape; they do not establish that a genuine game accepted or physically applied the production order.

open_questions: Will protected-pair native qualification confirm Append and empty Replace against a genuinely observed production queue?
What product behavior should replace the current fail-closed refusal if atomic nonempty Replace is later implemented?
